chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When the one in Ihram washes from major ritual impurity (Janabah), he pours (water) over his head and separates the hair with his fingers, part from part.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: How should a pilgrim in Ihram perform Ghusl for Janabah?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the practical application of the general prohibition against removing hair during Ihram, distinguishing between the act of removal and the mechanical action of washing. It establishes that while wringing or tightly combing the hair to remove loose strands is forbidden, gently separating strands with fingers to ensure water reaches the scalp is permissible, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of avoiding unnecessary hardship in ritual purity.
